# Post-1.1.1 Audit — Bug & Roadmap Backlog

Comprehensive audit of `ink-enhanced-select-input@1.1.1` (main @ `dc2b02b`).

**Baseline health:** 167 tests pass, `tsc` clean, `prettier --check` clean, `xo` clean, npm tarball
contains only the 7 intended files. The problems below are all things the current test suite does
**not** cover.

Every item marked **[verified]** was reproduced locally against `main` with a throwaway AVA test;
the observed output is quoted inline. Items marked **[static]** come from reading the source,
`package.json`, or Ink's internals without a runtime repro.

**IDs:** `B*` = bugs, `T*` = tooling/packaging, `F*` = features.
**Severity:** **P0** silent data loss / destructive action · **P1** wrong behaviour users will hit ·
**P2** rough edges · **P3** polish & forward-compat.

---

- [Bugs](#bugs)

## Bugs

### B1 — [P0] Ctrl+&lt;letter&gt; chords fire item hotkeys and vim navigation `bug`

**[verified]** Ink sets `input = keypress.name` when `keypress.ctrl` is true
(`ink/build/hooks/use-input.js`). The component compares `item.hotkey === input` and
`VERTICAL_NAV_KEYS.has(input)` without ever checking `key.ctrl`, so control chords are
indistinguishable from bare letters.

```tsx
<EnhancedSelectInput
  items={[
    { label: 'A', value: 'a' },
    { label: 'Danger', value: 'danger', hotkey: 'x' },
  ]}
  onSelect={(i) => console.log(i.label)}
/>
```

Pressing **Ctrl+X** (`\u0018`):

```
after Ctrl+X, selected = "Danger"   ← should be nothing
```

Pressing **Ctrl+K** (`\u000B`) on a 3-item list navigates up (wrapping `A` → `C`).

This is the highest-severity item in the audit: `Ctrl+C`/`Ctrl+D`/`Ctrl+W`/`Ctrl+X` are ordinary
terminal chords, and any app that maps a destructive action to a hotkey can be triggered by one.

**Fix:** require `!key.ctrl && !key.meta` (and probably `!key.shift` for the vim keys) before
matching vim navigation keys or item hotkeys. Add a `key.ctrl` guard to the hotkey `find`.

---

### B2 — [P1] Navigation keypresses arriving in the same tick are coalesced `bug`

**[verified]** `updateSelection` calls `setSelectedIndex(nextIndex)` with a value computed from the
render-scoped `selectedIndex`. Several keypresses delivered before React re-renders all read the
same stale closure value, so they collapse into a single move.

```
start = I0
after 3 same-tick ArrowDowns = I1   ← expected I3
```

The diagnosis is confirmed by the paths that *do* use functional updaters — they behave correctly
under the identical test:

| Handler | Update form | 3 same-tick presses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Navigation (`updateSelection`) | `setSelectedIndex(next)` | ❌ 1 move applied |
| Multi-select toggle | `setCheckedKeys(prev => …)` | ✅ all applied |
| Search input | `setSearchQuery(prev => …)` | ✅ all applied |

This affects held-down arrow keys (terminal key repeat), fast typists, `stdin` automation, and
anyone driving the component from a test harness.

This was reported externally in [PR #3](https://github.com/gfargo/ink-enhanced-select-input/pull/3)
by @hughescr and closed without merging; the underlying bug is still present. Worth crediting them
on the fix.

**Fix:** move the `findNextValidIndex` computation inside a functional updater, and derive
`rotateIndex` from `selectedIndex` (see also **B17**) so the two can't drift.

---

### B3 — [P0] `onConfirm` silently drops checked items hidden by the active search filter `bug`

**[verified]** `onConfirm` is built from `filteredItems`, not `items`:

```ts
const confirmed = filteredItems.filter((item) => checkedKeys.has(itemKey(item)))
```

So in `searchable` + `multiple` mode, anything the user checked before typing is discarded:

```
user checks Apple, checks Banana, types "cher", presses Enter
confirmed = []      ← both selections lost, no warning
```

`checkedKeys` still holds `apple` and `banana` — the data is right there, it's just filtered out on
the way to the callback. Silent data loss in the exact flow the two features were combined for.

Note the current test `searchable + multiple: can filter then confirm checked items` **asserts this
behaviour**, so it will need updating; it reads as though the truncation were intentional.

**Fix:** confirm from `items` (all checked items regardless of filter). If the current behaviour is
genuinely wanted somewhere, make it opt-in via something like `confirmScope: 'all' | 'filtered'`,
defaulting to `'all'`.

---

### B4 — [P1] `onHighlight` refires on every parent re-render when the callback is inline `bug`

**[verified]** The highlight effect lists the callback in its dependency array:

```ts
useEffect(() => { … onHighlight?.(highlightedItem) …
}, [selectedIndex, onHighlight, hasItems])
```

An inline arrow function — the overwhelmingly common way to pass this prop, and what the README
itself shows — is a new reference every render, so the effect re-runs every render:

```
onHighlight calls after mount: 1  →  after 5 parent re-renders: 6
```

A consumer that calls `setState` inside `onHighlight` gets an infinite render loop.

This is the same class of bug as [#17](https://github.com/gfargo/ink-enhanced-select-input/issues/17),
which was closed by removing `items` from the deps — but `onHighlight` itself was left in, so the
issue is only half fixed.

**Fix:** keep the callback in a ref (`onHighlightRef.current = onHighlight` in an effect) and depend
only on the values that represent an actual highlight change.

---

### B5 — [P1] `onHighlight` reports a stale item when filtering swaps the item at the same index `bug`

**[verified]** The highlight effect keys off `selectedIndex`. Typing in `searchable` mode resets the
index to `0` — but if it was *already* `0`, the effect never re-runs even though a completely
different item is now highlighted.

```tsx
<EnhancedSelectInput searchable items={[
  { label: 'Apple', value: 'apple' },
  { label: 'Banana', value: 'banana' },
]} onHighlight={(i) => seen.push(i.label)} />
```

```
initial highlights: ["Apple"]
after typing "b":   ["Apple"]     ← Banana is highlighted and rendered as such
```

The component renders `> Banana` while the last `onHighlight` the consumer received said `Apple`.
Any consumer driving a detail/preview pane off `onHighlight` shows the wrong content.

**Fix:** track the previously highlighted *item identity* (its `itemKey`) rather than its index, and
fire when that changes. Fixing this together with **B4** is natural — both are the same effect.

---

### B6 — [P1] Escape is swallowed on an empty list, so `onCancel` never fires `bug`

**[verified]** The early bail-out sits above the cancel handler:

```ts
if (!hasItems && !searchable) return
…
if (km.cancel && key.escape) { onCancel?.(); return }
```

```tsx
<EnhancedSelectInput items={[]} onCancel={() => setView('back')} />
```

```
cancelled after Escape on empty list = false
```

An empty list is exactly when a user most wants to back out ("no results, let me go back"), and
it's a normal transient state while items load. In a multi-step CLI flow they are simply stuck —
there is no key that does anything. An all-disabled list correctly *does* allow Escape, which makes
the inconsistency clearer.

**Fix:** handle Escape (and ideally the `keyMap`-gated global keys) before the `hasItems` guard.

---

### B7 — [P1] `onToggle` fires twice under React StrictMode `bug`

**[verified]** `onToggle` is invoked *inside* the `setCheckedKeys` updater:

```ts
setCheckedKeys((previous) => {
  …
  onToggle?.(item, nowChecked)   // side effect inside a state updater
  return next
})
```

React may invoke updaters more than once; StrictMode does so deliberately.

```
onToggle call count for ONE space press = 2  [true, true]
```

Consumers that log, POST, or increment a counter in `onToggle` double-fire. (Note the second call
reports `true` both times, so it isn't even a coherent toggle sequence.)

**Fix:** compute the next checked state outside the updater, call `setCheckedKeys` with the plain
value (or a pure updater), and invoke `onToggle` after — not within.

---

### B8 — [P1] Group headers are not counted against `limit`, so rendered height exceeds it `bug`

**[verified]** `limit` slices `filteredItems`, then headers are injected during render, so the
actual row count is `limit + <number of groups in the window>`.

```tsx
<EnhancedSelectInput limit={3} items={[
  { label: 'A', value: 'a', group: 'G1' },
  { label: 'B', value: 'b', group: 'G2' },
  { label: 'C', value: 'c', group: 'G3' },
  { label: 'D', value: 'd', group: 'G4' },
]} />
```

```
limit=3 but rendered 6 lines:
── G1 ──
> A
── G2 ──
  B
── G3 ──
  C
```

`limit` is documented as "Max number of visible items" and is the only tool for fitting a list into
a known terminal height. With groups it silently becomes unpredictable — double the requested
height in the worst case, which overflows the viewport and causes Ink to scroll/tear.

**Fix:** decide and document whether `limit` counts rows or items. Either budget headers into the
window when slicing, or add a separate `maxRows` prop.

---

### B9 — [P1] Non-contiguous items sharing a group render under the wrong header `bug`

**[verified]** Header suppression uses a "have I already rendered this group name?" `Set`, with no
awareness of adjacency:

```tsx
items={[
  { label: 'A', value: 'a', group: 'Alpha' },
  { label: 'B', value: 'b', group: 'Beta' },
  { label: 'C', value: 'c', group: 'Alpha' },
]}
```

```
── Alpha ──
> A
── Beta ──
  B
  C          ← C is in "Alpha" but renders inside the Beta section
```

The render actively lies about the data. Since the component never sorts or groups the array, any
consumer whose items aren't pre-sorted by group hits this.

The existing test `non-contiguous items with same group get separate headers per window` locks in
the buggy behaviour (its name says "separate headers", its assertion checks for one).

**Fix:** emit a header whenever `item.group !== previousVisibleItem.group` instead of tracking a
seen-set. Optionally also stable-sort items by group so a group can't be split at all.

---

### B10 — [P2] `defaultSelectedKeys` changes after mount are ignored `bug`

**[verified]** `useState(() => new Set(defaultSelectedKeys ?? []))` reads the prop exactly once.

```
initial defaultSelectedKeys=['a']       → [x] A / [ ] B
rerender with ['a','b']                 → [x] A / [ ] B   ← unchanged
```

Defensible for a prop named `default*`, but there is no controlled escape hatch, so
"select all", "restore saved selection", and "reset the form" are all impossible without remounting
via `key`. Should be documented at minimum. See **F1** for the controlled-mode proposal.

---

### B11 — [P2] `checkedKeys` retains entries for items that no longer exist `bug`

**[verified]** Nothing prunes `checkedKeys` when `items` changes.

```
check A, then remove A from items
checkedKeys = ["a"]     ← still there
```

Two consequences: `onConfirm` counts are computed against a set containing phantom keys, and if an
item with the same key returns later it silently comes back **pre-checked**. Likely in
search-as-you-type-over-remote-data flows.

**Fix:** intersect `checkedKeys` with the current item keys when `items` changes — or deliberately
keep them and document it as intentional (worth a `pruneCheckedKeys` prop if both behaviours are
wanted).

---

### B12 — [P2] `searchable` + `orientation="horizontal"` renders the search box inline `bug`

**[verified]** The search input is a direct child of the outer `Box`, whose `flexDirection` becomes
`row` in horizontal mode:

```
/ Search...> A    B
```

The prompt, cursor, and items are all mashed onto one line. The same applies to the
`showScrollIndicators` rows.

**Fix:** wrap the item row in its own `Box` and keep the search line in an outer column, so the
search prompt always sits above the items regardless of orientation.

---

### B13 — [P2] Forward-Delete deletes backwards in searchable mode `bug`

**[verified]** `key.backspace || key.delete` are handled identically:

```
query = "abc"
press forward-Delete (\u001B[3~)  →  "ab"
```

`\u007F` (what most terminals send for Backspace) maps to `key.delete` in Ink, so the `||` was
needed — but it also swallows the real Delete key. Cosmetic today; it becomes a genuine bug as soon
as the search field gets a movable cursor (**F3**).

**Fix:** distinguish the two once cursor support lands; for now, document it.

---

### B14 — [P2] `keyMap={{ select: false }}` + `searchable` inserts a carriage return into the query `bug`

**[verified]** With `select` disabled, `key.return` is no longer consumed, so Enter falls through to
the printable-character branch, which only guards `!key.ctrl && !key.meta`:

```
query after Enter with select disabled = "\r"
```

The query is now unmatchable and the stray `\r` corrupts the rendered prompt line.

**Fix:** exclude `key.return`/`key.tab` (and other non-printables) from the search-capture branch
explicitly rather than relying on earlier handlers to have consumed them.

---

### B15 — [P2] Duplicate-key dev warning spams the console on every re-render `bug`

**[verified]** The warning lives in an effect keyed on `[items, searchQuery]`; an inline `items`
array is a new reference every render.

```
warnings after mount: 1  →  after 4 re-renders: 5
```

React's own `Encountered two children with the same key` warning fires alongside it, so the console
gets two messages per render. A well-intentioned diagnostic becomes the noisiest thing in the
terminal — and it renders Ink output unreadable, since `console.warn` interleaves with the frame.

**Fix:** warn once per distinct duplicate-key set (`useRef` guard), and compare item keys by value
rather than array identity.

---

### B16 — [P2] Long labels wrap and break the fixed-height `limit` window `bug`

**[verified]** No truncation or width constraint is applied to labels.

```
limit=2 with one 200-char label → 4 rendered lines
```

Same practical consequence as **B8**: `limit` can't be relied on to bound the rendered height, so
lists overflow the terminal. Common with file paths, git branch names, and package descriptions.

**Fix:** see **F8** (`maxWidth` / truncation). At minimum document that `limit` counts items, not
rows.

---

### B17 — [P2] `limit` page-flips instead of scrolling; the cursor jumps to the top of the window `bug`

**[verified]** `rotateIndex = Math.floor(nextIndex / limit) * limit` snaps the window to fixed
page boundaries:

```
window 0:            after 3rd ArrowDown:
> Item0                > Item3
  Item1                  Item4
  Item2                  Item5
```

The entire viewport swaps at once and the highlight teleports from the bottom row to the top row.
Every comparable component (`ink-select-input`, `fzf`, `gum`) scrolls one row at a time and keeps
the cursor where the eye already is. This is the most visible UX difference from the ecosystem.

**Fix:** implement a cursor-following viewport — advance `rotateIndex` only when the cursor would
leave the window (optionally with a `scrollOffset`/padding). Worth a `paginationMode: 'page' |
'scroll'` prop if the current behaviour needs preserving. Best done alongside **B2**, since both
touch how `rotateIndex` is derived.

---

### B18 — [P3] `keyMap` has no flag for hotkeys — they're coupled to `select` `bug` `enhancement`

**[verified]** The hotkey branch is gated on `km.select`, so `keyMap={{ select: false }}` disables
Enter *and* all hotkeys, with no way to disable just one:

```
hotkey 'q' with keyMap.select=false → does not fire
```

Given that `keyMap` exists precisely to resolve conflicts with app-level keybindings, and
single-letter hotkeys are the most conflict-prone binding of all, this is the one flag most likely
to be wanted.

**Fix:** add `keyMap.hotkeys?: boolean` (default `true`), independent of `select`. Also consider
`keyMap.search` for the searchable capture branch.

---

### B19 — [P3] Kitty keyboard protocol key-release events are not filtered `bug`

**[static]** Ink 6.8 parses the Kitty keyboard protocol and forwards
`key.eventType: 'press' | 'repeat' | 'release'` to handlers without filtering
(`ink/build/hooks/use-input.js` line 70). This component ignores `eventType`, so on a
Kitty-protocol terminal with enhanced key reporting enabled, a single physical keypress can be
handled twice — once on press, once on release — double-navigating and double-toggling.

Not reproducible with `ink-testing-library` (it doesn't negotiate the protocol), hence **[static]**
and P3 — but it's cheap insurance and will matter as Kitty/Ghostty/WezTerm adoption grows.

**Fix:** early-return unless `key.eventType === undefined || key.eventType === 'press'` (allowing
`'repeat'` for navigation keys is a deliberate nicety).

---

### B20 — [P3] README documents type names that don't exist `documentation`

**[static]** The props table refers to `FC<IndicatorProps>`, `FC<ItemProps>`, and
`FC<GroupHeaderProps>`. The actual exports are `IndicatorProperties`, `ItemProperties`, and
`GroupHeaderProperties` — copy-pasting from the docs doesn't compile.

Also in the README's **Headless Hook** example:

```tsx
{visibleItems.map((item, i) => (
  <Text color={i === selectedIndex ? 'cyan' : undefined}>
```

`selectedIndex` is an index into the full filtered array while `i` indexes the *window* slice, so
the example highlights the wrong row (or none) whenever `limit` is set and `rotateIndex > 0`. The
correct comparison is `i + rotateIndex === selectedIndex`.

**Fix:** correct both. Consider exporting `Props`-suffixed aliases for ergonomics, and returning a
`selectedItem` from the hook (**F13**) so the example doesn't need index math at all.

## Packaging, tooling & CI

### T1 — [P0] `react` and `ink` must be `peerDependencies`, not `dependencies` `bug`

**[static]** Both are declared as hard `dependencies`. For a React component library this is a
packaging defect: a consumer whose own `ink`/`react` version doesn't dedupe gets a **second copy of
React** in `node_modules`, and hooks called across the two copies throw
`Invalid hook call` / `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useState')`. It also makes the
library silently override the app's Ink version.

**Fix:**

```jsonc
"peerDependencies": { "ink": ">=6", "react": ">=19" },
"peerDependenciesMeta": { … },
"devDependencies": { "ink": "^6.8.0", "react": "^19.2.0" }
```

Highest-impact packaging change here — worth a patch release on its own.

---

### T2 — [P1] Add Ink 7 support `enhancement`

**[static]** `ink@7.1.1` is published; this package allows `^6.0.0` only. Ink 7 raises the floor to
**Node >= 22** (this package says `>=20`), requires **react >= 19.2.0**, and adds a
`react-devtools-core` peer. Consumers on Ink 7 currently get a duplicated Ink install.

**Fix:** test against Ink 7, widen the peer range to `>=6` (or `^6 || ^7`), and document the
Node/React floors per Ink major in the compatibility table. Pairs naturally with **T1**.

---

### T3 — [P2] `package.json` is missing `repository`, `bugs`, `homepage`, and `keywords` `chore`

**[static]** Confirmed absent. npm therefore shows no repository link, no issue-tracker link, and
the package is undiscoverable by search for `ink`, `cli`, `select`, `prompt`, `tui`, `react`.
Cheapest possible win for adoption.

Also: `changelog.md` isn't in the published tarball (`npm pack --dry-run` shows 7 files, changelog
not among them) — worth including so the changelog is visible on npm.

---

### T4 — [P2] No `packageManager` field; Yarn v1 lockfile with an unpinned CI Yarn `chore`

**[static]** `yarn.lock` is `# yarn lockfile v1`, CI runs bare `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` with
`cache: yarn` and no version pin. Whatever Yarn the runner image ships decides the outcome — a
modern Yarn treats the v1 lockfile as a migration target and `--frozen-lockfile` is deprecated in
favour of `--immutable`. Reproduced locally: Yarn 4 immediately tried to migrate the lockfile and
failed the install.

**Fix:** add `"packageManager": "yarn@1.22.22"` (+ `corepack enable` in CI), or migrate to a modern
Yarn / npm and update the CI command accordingly.

---

### T5 — [P2] Dependency modernization `chore`

**[static]** `npm outdated` against `main`:

| Package | Current | Latest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prettier` | 2.8.8 | 3.9.6 |
| `xo` | 0.59.3 | 4.0.0 |
| `ava` | 6.4.1 | 8.0.1 |
| `@ava/typescript` | 5.0.0 | 7.0.0 |
| `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` | 4.6.2 | 7.1.1 |
| `release-it` | 17.11.0 | 20.2.1 |
| `@release-it/conventional-changelog` | 9.0.4 | 11.0.1 |
| `@types/node` | 22.20.1 | 26.1.1 |
| `typescript` | 5.9.3 | 7.0.2 |
| `ink` | 6.8.0 | 7.1.1 |

Two of these are more than cosmetic:

- **`eslint-plugin-react-hooks` v4 predates React 19.** v5+ is what actually flags the stale-closure
  and exhaustive-deps problems behind **B2**, **B4**, and **B5** — the linter that should have caught
  them is too old to do so. Note the source carries several
  `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` comments; each one is worth re-examining
  as part of this upgrade.
- **`prettier` 2 → 3** will reformat the repo; land it as an isolated commit so it doesn't pollute
  review of behavioural changes.

Best done as several small PRs rather than one sweep.

---

### T6 — [P2] CI hardening `chore`

**[static]** Current workflow is a single `lint-and-test` job on Node 20/22.

- Add **Node 24** to the matrix (and reconcile with the Ink 7 Node >= 22 floor, **T2**).
- Add an explicit typecheck step — `tsc` runs today only as a side effect of `pretest`, so a type
  regression surfaces as a confusing test failure.
- Add coverage reporting (`c8`) with a floor; the audit found ~20 real bugs against a 167-test
  suite, so measuring what's actually exercised is overdue.
- Add a **StrictMode** test pass — **B7** is invisible without one, and StrictMode double-invocation
  is the cheapest way to surface the remaining side-effect-in-updater problems.
- Add Dependabot/Renovate (would have surfaced **T2** and **T5** automatically).
- Move publishing into a release workflow with **npm provenance** (`--provenance`) instead of
  running `release-it` from a laptop.

---

### T7 — [P3] `.gitignore` hygiene `chore`

**[static]** Two problems:

- `docs` is ignored, so the **F14** docs directory would be silently untracked — a genuine trap.
- `dist` is listed twice (root-level entry plus the Nuxt block).

## Features & extensions

### F1 — Controlled mode `enhancement`

Add `selectedIndex` + `onIndexChange`, and `selectedKeys` + `onSelectedKeysChange` for multi-select,
alongside the existing uncontrolled props. Directly unblocks **B10** and makes "select all", "reset",
and persisted selections possible. The most-requested shape for a component like this and a
prerequisite for several items below.

### F2 — Custom filter / fuzzy matching / match highlighting `enhancement`

Today filtering is hard-coded to `label.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase())`. Add:

- `filter?: (item: Item<V>, query: string) => boolean` for full control
- optional fuzzy matching (subsequence scoring, `fzf`-style) behind `matchMode`
- searching additional fields (`item.value`, `description`, keywords)
- highlighting the matched substring in the rendered label

### F3 — Search field ergonomics `enhancement`

Real text-input behaviour in the search line: a movable cursor (←/→, Home/End, Ctrl+A/E), word
delete (Ctrl+W), clear line (Ctrl+U), and a visible cursor glyph. Also resolves **B13**.

### F4 — `onSearchChange`, controlled `searchQuery`, and async search `enhancement`

Expose the query to the parent so it can drive remote/async filtering; add `isLoading` with a
spinner/placeholder row and optional debounce. Turns the component into a live-search picker
(package search, branch picker, API lookup). Note this interacts with **B11** — prune or keep
checked keys as results churn.

### F5 — Select by value/key instead of index `enhancement`

`initialIndex` forces consumers to compute positions. Add `initialValue` / `initialKey` (and
`autoSelectFirstEnabled`). Removes a whole class of off-by-one bugs when items are sorted or
filtered upstream.

### F6 — `PageUp`/`PageDown` and configurable wrap-around `enhancement`

Add `keyMap.pageKeys` for PageUp/PageDown (Ink already surfaces `key.pageUp`/`key.pageDown`), plus
`loop?: boolean` (default `true`) to stop navigation clamping instead of wrapping — wrap-around is
disorienting in long lists.

### F7 — Multi-select quality of life `enhancement`

Select-all / select-none / invert (e.g. Ctrl+A, Ctrl+I) via `keyMap`; `minSelections` /
`maxSelections` with `onConfirm` blocked while invalid; a rendered `n selected` count; and
`checkedIndicator` customisation. Should land after **B3** and **F1**.

### F8 — Label truncation and width control `enhancement`

`maxWidth` / `truncate: 'end' | 'middle' | 'start'` so long labels ellipsize instead of wrapping.
Fixes **B16** and makes `limit` trustworthy as a height budget. Middle-truncation matters for file
paths.

### F9 — Secondary description lines and separator items `enhancement`

`item.description` / `item.hint` rendered dimmed beside or beneath the label (the standard
"command palette" look), and a `{ type: 'separator' }` item for visual rules without a group header.
Also `item.disabledReason` to explain why a row is unselectable.

### F10 — Group improvements `enhancement`

Sticky group header when a group is scrolled mid-window, `collapsible` groups (Space/→ to
fold/unfold), explicit `groups` ordering, a "continued" affordance when a group spans a page
boundary, and group-level select-all in multi-select mode. Should follow **B8** and **B9**, which
fix the foundations.

### F11 — Auto-generated help / footer hint line `enhancement`

`showHelp` (or `footer`) rendering the currently active keybindings — `↑↓ navigate · space toggle ·
enter confirm · esc cancel` — derived from `keyMap`, `multiple`, and `searchable` so it can never
drift from actual behaviour. Big discoverability win, especially since vim keys and hotkeys are
otherwise invisible.

### F12 — Theming and `NO_COLOR` `enhancement`

A `theme` prop for the colours currently hard-coded in the default components (`green`, `gray`),
plus honouring the [`NO_COLOR`](https://no-color.org/) convention. Today restyling requires
replacing all three render components.

### F13 — Headless hook ergonomics `enhancement`

`useEnhancedSelectInput` currently returns raw indices. Add `selectedItem`, `filteredItems`,
`windowIndex` (window-relative, removing the `i + rotateIndex` arithmetic that the README gets wrong
in **B20**), and imperative setters (`setSelectedIndex`, `setSearchQuery`, `toggle`) for custom
keybindings. Consider a `./headless` subpath export.

### F14 — Docs & examples `documentation`

A runnable `examples/` directory (one file per feature, `node examples/multi-select.js`) — currently
the only executable demo is the storybook, which requires a full build. Plus a proper docs site with
recorded terminal casts (asciinema/VHS), a migration note for the v1 keyboard changes, and a
recipes section (wizard flows, remote search, nested menus). Note **T7**: `.gitignore` currently
ignores `docs`.

### F15 — Type-ahead jump in non-searchable mode `enhancement`

Standard listbox behaviour: typing `d`,`e` jumps to the first item starting with "de" without
entering a filter mode, with a short idle timeout resetting the buffer. Complements rather than
replaces `searchable`. Needs care against the hotkey system (see **B18**).

### F16 — Ink focus-manager integration `enhancement`

`isFocused` is a manual boolean today. Offer opt-in integration with Ink's `useFocus`/`focusManager`
(e.g. `autoFocus` / `focusId`) so multiple selects on one screen can Tab between each other without
the parent hand-rolling focus state.

### F17 — Nested / submenu (tree) support `enhancement`

`item.children` for drill-down menus, with →/Enter to descend, ←/Escape to ascend, and a breadcrumb.
The storybook already hand-rolls this pattern with `useState` views, which is evidence it belongs in
the library. Large — likely a `2.0` candidate.

### F18 — Large-list performance `enhancement`

Add a benchmark for 10k+ items. Current per-render work is `O(n)` several times over (filter, group
scan, duplicate-key scan on every `items` change). Confirm the `limit` window keeps render cost
bounded and memoize the filter.

### Existing tests that need attention

Two tests actively assert buggy behaviour and must be **rewritten** as part of the fix rather than
treated as regressions:

| Test | Issue |
| --- | --- |
| `searchable + multiple: can filter then confirm checked items` | **B3** — asserts `confirmed.length === 1` after filtering, i.e. locks in the data loss |
| `non-contiguous items with same group get separate headers per window` | **B9** — name says "separate headers", assertion checks for exactly one |

One further test is worth a note: `searchable: selection resets to first item when query changes`
passes legitimately (it moves the cursor to index 1 first, so the index really does change), but it
reads as though highlight tracking under filtering were covered — which is what let **B5** through.
Worth adding the index-stays-at-0 case beside it.
